summary: Concurrent signed-URL refresh microservice causing short-lived token burst and tenant 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DataSort Inc.) reports sudden 429 spikes for a subset of API keys over the last 18 hours. Spike correlates with a background service that refreshes signed URLs for archived embedding files. Impact: multiple ingestion pipelines see repeated 429s for short durations (~20-60s), causing downstream backfills to fail and triggering support SLA.

Observed behavior:
- 429s appear in waves across many clients that share the same tenant, not all API keys.
- Requests are clustered around file download and file-metadata endpoints used by the signed-url refresher.
- Throttle headers indicate token window exhaustion on the tenant layer (tenant token-bucket) despite per-key accounting showing low steady usage.

Customer impact:
- Backfill jobs fail with exponential retry amplification.
- ML feature pipelines lag by 2–6 hours.

Business impact:
- Enterprise customer on an SLA contract; needs root cause and mitigation within 48 hours.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a worker that calls PUT /v1/files/refresh-signed-url for N objects with no jitter in a tight loop.
2) Use 200 short-lived API keys (rotate per worker) tied to the same tenant.
3) Trigger a simultaneous refresh cycle across workers.
4) Observe 429s returned from API gateway and tenant-level throttle metrics incrementing in bursts.
logs:
Selected log excerpts (redacted keys):

- 2026-03-10T11:22:12Z rate-limiter DEBUG tenant_bucket_account tenant=dsinc added=+450 counted=+450 total_window=1000ms
- 2026-03-10T11:22:13Z proxy-pool INFO backend=fileservice node=files-12 request_id=abcd123 cohort_size=180
- 2026-03-10T11:22:50Z worker[dsinc-refresh] ERROR retry attempt=6 last_status=429 message="exponential backoff triggered"
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Health checks or monitoring probes incrementing tenant quota (low likelihood; probe traffic pattern doesn't match).
- Duplicate accounting from proxy pool fanout where a single logical refresh is translated into parallel backend requests and each is double-counted at tenant layer.
- Short-lived API key rotation causing many fresh keys to bypass per-key smoothing and hit tenant token window simultaneously.

Findings:
- Rate-limiter tracing shows the tenant-level refill is applied per proxy connection, and our proxy-pool spread (cohort_size ~180) produced near-simultaneous accounting updates.
- Auth logs confirm ~150 distinct ephemeral keys created by the customer's refresh service in a 15s window.
- Downstream backoff logic in the customer's worker is aggressive (no jitter), causing burst amplification.
- Console metrics: tenant_burst_count spike aligns exactly with signed-url refresh schedule (cron at HH:22).

Temporary mitigation performed:
- Applied a 30-minute tenant quota bump to prevent further production impact (noted in billing).
- Instructed customer to enable jitter and reduce parallelism to <=8 workers per refresh job.

resolution:
Workaround and short-term fix:
- Customer implemented jittered backoff and reduced parallelism; immediate reduction in burst 429s observed.
- Support applied temporary tenant quota increase until permanent fix deployed.
Permanent fix and follow-up:
- Merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1284 to ensure proxy-pool fanout updates aggregate for tenant accounting instead of naive per-connection increments (deployed to prod us-east 2026-03-12 02:45 UTC).
- Added server-side smoothing for ephemeral-key bursts (smoothing window increased from 500ms to 2s for tenant layer).
- Created runbook entry and a new alert rule for high short-window tenant bursts.
- Billing note: temporary quota bump recorded and will be reconciled with customer finance.

Follow-ups (action items):
- Engineering to verify no regression in per-route fairness after smoothing (owner: Priya Menon, due 2026-03-20).
- Product to propose console UX to show "ephemeral-key burst detection" for enterprise tenants (owner: Leila Chen, due 2026-04-01).
